reason: The hypothesis directly restates the mechanism, intervention, and predicted outcome from P9, P23, P25, and P26, which already report that nanosegregation of Ni, Cr, and Mn to grain boundaries causes ductility loss and that pre-existing Cr-rich precipitates can mitigate this. The proposed test is a straightforward replication of the comparison already performed in P9, with no new alloy, regime, or mechanistic insight.
copied_elements: GB segregation of Ni, Cr, Mn reduces cohesion and causes intergranular cracking (P12, P23, P26)
GB segregation engineering via pre-existing Cr-rich precipitates to evade ductility loss (P9, P25)
Ductility loss at intermediate temperatures in single-phase fcc HEA (P12, P23)
Comparative testing at room temperature vs. intermediate temperatures (P9, P12)
